item.title: Hokkaido Bear Watching Guide: Where & How to See Brown Bears
item.description: Hokkaido is home to the Ezo brown bear (higuma), Japan’s largest land animal, plus a rich cast of northern wildlife — deer, red foxes, Steller’s sea eagles, red-crowned cranes and whales. Seeing a wild brown bear is a genuine thrill, and Hokkaido offers some of Japan’s best opportunities to do so safely and responsibly, above all from boat cruises along the Shiretoko coast where bears forage on the shore. For guaranteed sightings, well-run bear parks let families get close.

item.title: Shiretoko Peninsula Guide: UNESCO Nature, Cruises & Bears
item.description: Jutting into the Sea of Okhotsk at Hokkaido’s far northeast, the Shiretoko Peninsula is one of Japan’s last great wildernesses — a UNESCO World Heritage site where primeval forest, volcanic peaks and a wild coast of cliffs and waterfalls shelter an extraordinary density of wildlife. This is brown bear country, home also to deer, foxes, eagles and, offshore, whales and seals. Explore the Shiretoko Five Lakes, take a nature cruise beneath sea cliffs, and in late winter watch drift ice pack the shore.

item.title: Hokkaido Nature Guide: Shiretoko, Daisetsuzan, Furano & Kushiro
item.description: Hokkaido’s nature operates on a scale that Japan’s other islands cannot match. The island is 83,000 square kilometres — roughly the size of Austria — and contains 6 national parks, including Japan’s largest (Daisetsuzan) and one of its two UNESCO World Heritage natural sites (Shiretoko). The wildlife is genuinely wild: brown bears that fish for salmon in rivers accessible from the road, red-crowned cranes that are among the world’s rarest birds, and an autumn foliage season that begins 3–4 weeks before the rest of Japan.
